title: World Bank’s role in Oman’s Vision 2040
gist: Oman's Vision 2040 targets cutting hydrocarbons from ~30% of GDP to 8.4% by 2040; strong fiscal repair (debt 69% to 38.5% of GDP) and IFC-led deals like the $1.6bn Duqm-area polysilicon plant showcase diversification, with the World Bank Group positioning to mobilise private capital.

insights.claim: Oman aims to cut hydrocarbons' share of GDP from about 30% today (two-thirds of fiscal revenue and over 60% of exports) to 16% by 2030 and 8.4% by 2040.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Aggressive diversification targets imply large non-oil investment flows; watch progress vs the 2030 16% milestone.
insights.locator: It aims to cut hydrocarbons’ share

insights.claim: Oman needs over 100,000 additional jobs for nationals by 2040, which the public sector cannot provide; private-sector employment of Omanis rose to 54% in 2024 from roughly a third a few years earlier.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Labor nationalisation pressure affects private-sector hiring costs in Oman.
insights.locator: Strengthening the private sector is central

insights.claim: Private-sector investment, currently just over half of GDP, needs to rise toward a 70% target by 2040 to sustain diversification as hydrocarbon revenues decline.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Signals continued investor-friendly reforms and incentives for FDI.

insights.claim: Oman's economy grew 2.6% in 2025, driven largely by non-oil activity, with inflation averaging 0.9%, among the lowest in the GCC.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Low-inflation, non-oil-led growth supports Omani sovereign credit.

insights.claim: Oman posted a fiscal surplus of 0.7% of GDP in 2025 and cut public debt from nearly 69% of GDP in 2020 to 38.5% by 2025.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Rapid deleveraging underpins rating upgrades and tighter Omani sovereign spreads.

insights.claim: Oman is projected to run a current account surplus of 3.4% in 2026, with central bank reserves of $19.3 billion at end-2025 covering about four months of imports.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: External buffers support the riyal peg.

insights.claim: Near-term risks to Oman include regional tensions and softer tourism inflows.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Geopolitical spillovers remain the key tail risk for Omani assets.

insights.claim: The UK became Oman's largest foreign investor in 2025 at $42 billion, followed by the US and UAE, as regulatory reforms attracted new investment.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Western capital leads Omani FDI; UK firms most exposed.

insights.claim: Oman's new $1.6 billion polysilicon plant, the region's largest, began operations in January 2026 and will ramp to 100,000 tons a year based on market demand, enough for 40 GW of solar modules.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: New non-Chinese polysilicon capacity matters for solar supply-chain diversification and pricing.

insights.claim: IFC led the polysilicon financing with $250 million ($200 million long-term debt, $50 million equity) and mobilised $713 million from DFIs, investors and local banks, while Future Fund Oman, the largest shareholder, invested $260 million.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Sovereign and DFI backing de-risks the project; model for GCC industrial deals.

insights.claim: Ramp-up of the Omani polysilicon plant to full capacity is explicitly contingent on market demand.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Global polysilicon oversupply could delay utilisation; watch ramp pace as a demand signal.
insights.quote: expected to ramp up to 100,000 tons based on market demand

insights.claim: A new World Bank Group country office in Muscat opened in 2025 combining IBRD, IFC and MIGA to coordinate finance mobilisation and de-risking.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: More DFI co-investment and guarantees likely for Omani projects.

insights.claim: MIGA issued $1.7 billion in 15-year guarantees in 2019 for seven infrastructure projects in the Duqm Special Economic Zone, expanding logistics and export capacity.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Duqm is Oman's anchor logistics/industrial hub benefiting from political-risk cover.
